children: , China's commerce and cloud-AI giant, set an aggressive target of more than 20 gigawatts of global data-center capacity by 2032. U.S.-listed shares climbed approximately 3.2% to $119.43, keeping investors focused on how quickly Alibaba is turning its AI ambitions into physical infrastructure.

Reuters reported that Alibaba is developing an AI model with between five trillion and 10 trillion parameters while preparing its Zhenwu V900 accelerator for commercial availability in early 2027. The chip is expected to deliver roughly three times the performance of its predecessor, while Alibaba is designing clusters capable of scaling toward 500,000 chips. The message is clear: Alibaba does not want to rent its way into the AI race. It wants control of the model, the silicon and the cloud capacity underneath it.

That strategy comes with a huge capital bill. Twenty gigawatts equals 20,000 megawatts of potential data-center capacity, so utilization and customer demand will eventually matter as much as headline scale. The valuation picture remains relatively restrained: the chart shows Alibaba at $119.43 versus a GF Value estimate of $121.27, leaving the shares about 1.52% below GF Value. That narrow discount suggests the market is already giving Alibaba meaningful credit for its AI push, while still waiting for the spending to translate into durable cloud growth and returns on capital.

title: Alibaba Gains 3.2% as 20 Gigawatts Unite Chips, Models and Cloud
